subject: Mathematics
title: Circles
summary: A circle is the locus of points at a fixed distance (radius) from a fixed point (centre). The general equation x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 has centre (−g, −f) and radius √(g² + f² − c).
The position of a point or line relative to a circle is decided by S₁ = x₁² + y₁² + 2gx₁ + 2fy₁ + c and by comparing distance from the centre with the radius.
Tangent, normal, chord of contact, length of tangent, common tangents, family of circles and orthogonal circles are the main JEE tools.

formulas.name: Standard and general form
formulas.formula: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²;  x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 → centre (−g, −f), r = √(g² + f² − c)
formulas.note: A real circle needs g² + f² − c ≥ 0.

formulas.name: Diameter form
formulas.when: Circle on the join of two points as diameter.

formulas.name: Parametric form
formulas.formula: x = h + r cos θ, y = k + r sin θ

formulas.name: Position of a point
formulas.formula: S₁ > 0 outside;  S₁ = 0 on;  S₁ < 0 inside

formulas.name: Line and circle
formulas.formula: distance p of centre from line: p > r no intersection;  p = r tangent;  p < r secant;  chord length = 2√(r² − p²)

formulas.name: Tangent condition
formulas.formula: y = mx + c touches x² + y² = a² iff c² = a²(1 + m²);  tangent: y = mx ± a√(1 + m²)

formulas.name: Tangent at a point
formulas.formula: T = 0: xx₁ + yy₁ + g(x + x₁) + f(y + y₁) + c = 0
formulas.when: Tangent at (x₁, y₁) on the circle.

formulas.name: Chord of contact and midpoint chord
formulas.formula: chord of contact from (x₁, y₁): T = 0;  chord with midpoint (x₁, y₁): T = S₁

formulas.name: Two circles
formulas.formula: d > r₁ + r₂: 4 common tangents;  d = r₁ + r₂: 3;  |r₁ − r₂| < d < r₁ + r₂: 2;  d = |r₁ − r₂|: 1;  d < |r₁ − r₂|: 0

formulas.name: Family of circles
formulas.formula: S + λL = 0 (circle and line);  S₁ + λS₂ = 0 (two circles);  radical axis S₁ − S₂ = 0

examples.title: Centre and radius
examples.problem: Find the centre and radius of x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 12 = 0.

examples.title: Length of tangent
examples.problem: Length of the tangent from (7, 2) to the circle above?

examples.title: Chord length
examples.problem: A line is at distance 3 from the centre of x² + y² = 25. Chord length?

examples.title: Common tangents
examples.problem: Circles of radii 3 and 4 have centres 10 apart. Number of common tangents?

examples.title: Tangent with given slope
examples.problem: Tangents to x² + y² = 9 with slope 1?

examples.title: Circle through three points
examples.solution: c = 0; through (2, 0): 4 + 4g = 0 ⇒ g = −1; through (0, 4): 16 + 8f = 0 ⇒ f = −2. Equation: x² + y² − 2x − 4y = 0 (centre (1, 2), radius √5).

topics.title: Conditions for a general second-degree equation to be a circle
topics.explain: ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 is a circle if a = b ≠ 0 and h = 0 (and the radius is real).

topics.title: Normal to a circle
topics.explain: Every normal passes through the centre. The normal at (x₁, y₁) is the line joining (x₁, y₁) and the centre.

topics.title: Director circle
topics.explain: The locus of points from which perpendicular tangents are drawn to x² + y² = a² is x² + y² = 2a².

topics.title: Radical axis and centre
topics.explain: The radical axis is the locus of points with equal tangent lengths to two circles: S₁ − S₂ = 0, perpendicular to the line of centres. Three circles' radical axes meet at the radical centre.

topics.title: Angle between circles
topics.explain: cos θ = (r₁² + r₂² − d²)/(2r₁r₂), where θ is the angle between radii at a point of intersection; θ = 90° gives the orthogonality condition.

topics.title: Common chord
topics.explain: The common chord of two intersecting circles is S₁ − S₂ = 0; its length uses the distance from either centre.

ratta: y = mx ± a√(1 + m²) tangent to x² + y² = a².
Common tangents: 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 as circles move closer.
